feedback: If the child still subtracts digits, return to the clock: show the 60 minutes in the hour and count the jumps to and past the o'clock.
Check the 14:45 + 40 min answer: 14:45→15:00 is 15 min, then 25 more to 15:25.
Check the 'next service 25 minutes later' answer: from 10:50, count 10:50→11:00 is 10 min, then 15 more to 11:15, so it leaves at 11:15.
activities.intendedInsight: The digits after the colon are minutes out of 60, not tenths of an hour, so durations must be counted in minutes, not read as decimals.
learnerActions: When a journey duration has been found by subtracting clock times as if they were decimals (e.g. 11:20 − 10:50 written as 0.70, or '70 minutes'), look at an analogue clock and state how many minutes are in one hour (60).
Find the correct duration in minutes by counting on from the start time to the end time across the hour on the clock face or an empty number line (e.g. 10:50 → 11:00 → 11:20 = 30 minutes).
Try a journey that crosses the hour in the other direction too — e.g. a train leaving at 14:45 with a 40-minute journey: when does it arrive?
Combine a lookup with a forward duration: if the next service is 25 minutes later than the one shown (say it leaves at 10:50), count on to find its departure time rather than adding digits.
activities.title: Confront time-as-decimal with an analogue clock

feedback: A cross-the-hour duration item surfaces decimal subtraction (0.70/'70') versus a correct 30 minutes — if wrong, return to counting on across the hour.
A 'how many more' item surfaces reading a single value instead of a difference — if wrong, point to both values and subtract.
activities.intendedInsight: The reading-and-calculating procedure can be checked against items deliberately chosen to catch time-as-decimal and read-off-instead-of-difference errors.
learnerActions: Find a departure time from a shown timetable (selecting from options).
Complete 'the journey from A to B takes ___ minutes', including at least one item where the arrival crosses the hour (e.g. 10:50→11:20).
Complete or fill a missing cell in a two-way table.
Answer one 'how many more' item that requires a difference, not a single value.
activities.title: Scorable checks on lookups, durations and cell completion
